absent: Behavior of locks iteration start, next and show handlers and iterator layout
Acquisition side of blocked-lock exclusion and file table protection for locks listing
Generic proc sequence operations and file inode operations beyond wiring
Dynamic inode number base, allocation limits and identifier reuse policy
Proc entry flag bit values and permanent entry semantics
Force lookup propagation effects on path resolution and net namespace interaction
File lock, lease and context object layouts and notifier chain behavior
Mbcache entry object layout, key and value widths, and flag bit assignments
Hash function properties and reference wakeup mechanism
Shrinker registration, pressure propagation and workqueue scheduling guarantees
User and group translation table layouts, extent representation and mapping helpers
Mount namespace sequence, event, notification and visibility semantics
Mountpoint hash, dentry lifetime and cover list management

findings.text: Proc infrastructure exposes creation of sequence-backed files with caller-supplied operations and state size, registration of entries under a parent, release of entry storage, allocation and release of dynamic identities, and inheritance of ownership from parent to child.
A shared helper converts a bounded name to an unsigned integer for numeric proc directory handling, allowing callers to detect non-numeric input through a sentinel result.

Mbcache exposes creation and destruction of cache instances plus creation, exact and reusable lookup, conditional removal, liveness waiting, recency marking and final release of entries, providing a reusable key-value cache with pressure-driven reclaim.
Mount identity handling exposes allocation of a mapping from a user namespace and enumeration of user or group translations for status reporting relative to the caller.

Admission of new proc names refuses empty input, overlong input, single dot, double dot, direct numeric children of the root and children of permanently empty directories, with no observable allocation on refusal.

Sibling entries under a proc directory follow a total order by name length first and bytewise content second, used consistently for both locating an existing child and deciding placement of a new child.

Creation of regular proc files supplies a regular file type when absent and broad readability when no permission bits are given, while declining modes that are not regular files and binding successful entries to generic file handling with caller data.

Per-entry capability marking mirrors the associated operations vector, propagating permanence and the availability of read, compat control and seek support where present and leaving other entries unmarked.

Successful registration provides a fresh dynamic identity and at most one visible entry per name under a parent, with duplicate attempts refused and partial identity or storage released so failures leave no visible residue.

A successfully created proc entry carries copied name storage using inline capacity when the name fits, the requested mode and link count, an empty child collection, a single initial reference, initialized unload exclusion and opener tracking, ownership copied from the parent, and inherited forced lookup where the parent requires it.

Resolution of slash-separated proc paths proceeds through existing intermediate directories under shared protection and yields the parent directory plus the final component, reporting failure when an intermediate component is absent.
Decimal name parsing accepts only canonical forms without leading zeros, accumulating value with overflow protection and returning an all-ones sentinel for empty, non-decimal or overflowing input.
Release of a proc entry frees link-attached data when the entry is a link, frees separately allocated names while leaving inline names alone, and then frees the entry object itself.
Mbcache bucket choice derives from the entry key hashed under the cache-configured table width, directing all hash membership operations for that key to the same bucket.

Translation table copying requires a previously established source, copies small inline tables directly and duplicates both directional extent arrays for large tables, reporting invalid sources or allocation failures without exposing partial state.

Status enumeration presents mount translations relative to the caller identity mapping and includes only ranges fully resolvable there, separating successive mappings with a delimiter and accounting output growth.

Parent lookup for proc path handling runs under shared directory protection while insertion of a new child runs under exclusive protection, ensuring stable traversal during concurrent creation and unique placement.

Mbcache guards the global recency list and occupancy count with a dedicated spin lock and guards hash membership with per-bucket bit locks, using an extra transient reference during setup so list handling need not nest inside bucket handling.
Completion of locks listing releases the global blocked-lock spin exclusion and then the file table write protection, matching the acquisition held across iteration.

Each proc entry carries its own unload exclusion initialized at creation alongside opener tracking, and each processor carries its own file lock list with dedicated spin protection initialized during subsystem startup.

A cache instance comprises a hash table pointer, a table width exponent, a maximum occupancy bound, a spin lock guarding a recency list and live count, the count itself, a shrinker handle and a background work item for deferred reclaim.

A mount namespace object combines common namespace state, a root mount, an ordered mount collection with cached ends, owning user context and counters, a wait queue, origin and event sequences, optional notification state, a visible-mount set, mount totals with pending count, a passive reference tally and an anonymity marker, with randomized layout.

Per-processor mount accounting holds get and put tallies with a writer count, while a mountpoint object links its dentry through hash linkage and tracks both mounted users that pin it and covers of unmounted parents.

A mount identity object pairs a user translation table with a group translation table under a shared reference count, with two globally available singly referenced instances denoting the neutral and invalid mappings.
Locks display wiring binds a sequence interface to dedicated handlers for starting, advancing, finishing and rendering iteration, used with per-iteration private state sized for a locks iterator.

Proc file establishment moves from path splitting to name validation to object allocation to registration to visibility, with any refusal or allocation failure aborting before visibility and releasing partial resources.

An entry moves from allocation with dual protection references to hashed and listed membership, then through referenced and shared states driven by touch and lookup, toward reclaimable or explicitly removed states ending in hash detachment and storage release.

Cache occupancy management rests in normal operation below the bound, requests deferred reclaim once the bound is reached and performs immediate bounded reclaim when occupancy grows far beyond the bound, with pressure callbacks also driving count reporting and scanning.

Reusable search begins anew without a cursor or continues after a supplied cursor, examines only same-key reusable candidates with live references under bucket protection, and hands ownership of the new reference to the caller while releasing the prior cursor.
Early initialization publishes the kernel lock listing as a sequence-backed proc file with iterator-sized private state, making lock information available once proc is ready.
File locking startup establishes object caches for contexts, locks and leases, initializes per-processor lock lists with their spin protection, and prepares the lease notification chain.
Mbcache module startup creates a reclaim-accounted object cache for entries and reports allocation failure, with module exit destroying that cache after all instances are gone.

Instance setup sizes the hash from a caller exponent, derives the occupancy bound, initializes list and locks and buckets, registers pressure callbacks and prepares deferred work, while teardown cancels work, frees pressure handling and requires prior quiescence before freeing remaining members and storage.
Concurrent or repeated creation with the same name under one parent risks duplicate registration, which is detected under exclusion and refused with a diagnostic rather than creating an alias.

Destroying a cache while entries remain referenced or destroying the entry slab while instances exist risks use after free, so callers must ensure no cache use remains and entries are unshared before teardown.

Attempting to derive a mount mapping from an unwritten user namespace table fails cleanly, and partial failure while populating user and group tables releases the partially built mapping rather than exposing it.

Status reporting may encounter output exhaustion while formatting or separating mappings, in which case it signals retry instead of emitting truncated data, and unmappable ranges are silently omitted.
The synchronous reclaim batch size is sixty four entries.
The background reclaim divisor is sixteen, used to derive deferred work size from maximum occupancy.
